name: Potter's Wheel
summary: Throw a pot on a spinning wheel: drag the clay wall in or out, then glaze it and fire it in a kiln
about: A calm pottery studio with a hanging lamp, a shelf of fired pots and a turning wheel, where the clay is drawn like a real lathe form with specks that ride round with the spin, and keeps its volume: press it in and it grows taller, pull it out and it squats down. Open the top, pick a glaze such as cobalt with white flowers, and a brick kiln hood comes down, heats to 1240 degrees and lifts to show a glossy pot that flies to your shelf. Good for a crafts or ceramics shop, a mindful break page or a portfolio header.
how: Press on the wall of the spinning clay and drag it in to make it taller and slimmer, or out to make it wider.
Press Raise to draw the walls up, Open to press a hollow and a rim into the top, and New clay to start over.
With the keyboard, focus the wheel: up and down pick a height, left presses in and right pulls out.
Pick a glaze and press Glaze & fire: dip, kiln hood, heat, cool and a glossy reveal before it joins the shelf.
Set the spin speed with the slider; reduced motion keeps every step without the wobble, squash and sparkles.
